page: Amazon Web Services r6i.24xlarge is a high-density, memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processors operating on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at up to 3.5 GHz. The configuration provides 768 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. CPU instruction support includes AVX-512, alongside dedicated cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes 38 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local NVMe storage, and has no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects strong multi-threaded performance and high memory bandwidth. Multi-core compute evaluations place the instance in the top 25%, recording 92,919.38 on stress-ng, 17,594.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and 75,974.79 on PassMark CPU. PassMark CPU encryption scores reach the top 10% tier at 87,330.18, aided by dedicated cryptographic extensions. The memory subsystem sustains 315.34 GB/sec read and 137.83 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks. This translates to strong performance in high-throughput workloads, including 84.83 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 63.89 GB/sec on static web serving benchmarks. Single-core performance remains in the middle 50% across Geekbench and stress-ng, while large language model generation on 70B parameter models falls in the bottom 25% due to the lack of dedicated accelerator hardware.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the r6i.24xlarge offers high memory density and balanced multi-core throughput for platforms that require expansive RAM without the expense of GPU-accelerated silicon. The absence of ephemeral local storage requires reliance on network-attached EBS volumes for persistent state, which consumes part of the 38 Gbps pipeline. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise environments, including distributed in-memory databases like Redis and Memcached, large relational database management systems, data caching tiers, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores on Intel Xeon 8375C processors, built on the AWS Nitro System. It provides 768 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, a 38 Gbps baseline network interface, no bundled local storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile multi-core processing, strong memory throughput of 315.34 GB/sec for uncached reads, and top-decile hardware encryption capabilities. Practical throughput tests confirm its memory efficiency, achieving 84.83 million Redis SET operations per second and strong relational database metrics. Although single-core throughput is moderate and large LLM generation is limited without GPU acceleration, the hardware profile offers exceptional compute and memory density for large in-memory caches, distributed databases, real-time analytics, and enterprise transactional systems.
